newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-WYLLIE TO COACH PUMAS, MORDT TAKES TRANSVAAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WYLLIE TO COACH PUMAS, MORDT TAKES TRANSVAAL.

text.p: Springbok selector Ray Mordt has replaced Alex Wyllie as Transvaal coach, rugby officials said on Monday.
Wyllie had already accepted an offer to help coach Argentina when they host South African in November but had been keen to see out his contract with Transvaal until the end of the season.

But Transvaal chief executive Johan Prinsloo told a news conference: "We have decided to put a more professional management structure together and after discussions with Mr Wyllie he decided not to be part of that new structure."
The replacement is seen as making the former All Black coach pay the price for failing to revive flagging Transvaal fortunes in a sometimes stormy six months in office.

Mordt, who takes over with immediate effect, was replaced by Wyllie during the Super 12 competition in April amid controversy. Wyllie's appointment was leaked by a New Zealand television commentator when Transvaal were abroad, before Mordt had been contacted by his own union.

The former assistant Springbok coach said that he was happy to be back at the reins, but said his new appointment would mean he would not have time to coach the South African A team which tours Britain in November and December.
Wyllie's assistant, Hugo van As, remains part of the new structure as the backline assistant coach. Transvaal stalwart Tito Lupini will help out with the forwards.
